title: Operator pocket play slate and incident-ready binder
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact operator "pocket" slate intended for on-shift engineers running cutovers (canary->gradual->full). Short, punchy, and actionable — not a full playbook. Use this during the 72h window around a release to make fast, consistent decisions and speed handoffs.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to model-serving and routing changes, infra config flips, and API surface tweaks that affect latency/availability.
- We assume default observability stacks (Console dashboards, Lightstep traces, and token-level cost probes) are available.
- Primary channels: Slack #release-ops, PagerDuty (oncall:release), and the Release Night Zoom bridge.

Quick reference: who to page
- Primary on-call: release-oncall (See PagerDuty)
- Release lead: Ravi Patel
- Infra/surge: Sofia Alvarez
- MLOps/model routing: Noah Williams

Pre-cutover (T-72 to T-1h) checklist — quick checks (tick off)
- [ ] Confirm calendar and shift coverage: names for T-72/T-24/T-0 handoffs in doc header
- [ ] Validate feature flags exist and map to rollout lanes (canary, 10%, 50%, 100%)
- [ ] Confirm canary shard and traffic steering policy (policy id + target hosts)
- [ ] Sanity run: smoke test suite on staging prod-mirror (list below)
- [ ] Token/quota guardrails set (per-customer rate limits, burst caps)
- [ ] Backup model variant available for immediate fallback (quantized/cheaper variant)
- [ ] Confirm roll-forward and rollback steps are scripted and have tested playbooks

Cutover day quick tempo (T-0 -> +24h)
- T-0: Switch canary lane (0.5% traffic) -> observe 30m
- T+30m: Check signals; if green, step to 5% -> observe 45m
- T+1h30m: If green, step to 25% -> observe 1h
- T+2h30m: 50% -> observe 2h
- T+4h30m: 100% (if all prior gates pass)
Notes: be conservative if any critical customers on canary shard. Use staggered region lifts if needed.

Signal thresholds (fast sanity gate)
- API error-rate (5xx) spike: if > 0.25% absolute increase over baseline AND sustained for 3m -> HOLD or ROLLBACK
- p95 latency: if increase > 60% relative to baseline and > 1500ms absolute -> HOLD
- Token burn (tokens/sec): if > 2x expected for the canary population -> investigate prompt/traffic regressions
- CPU/GPU saturation on pool: if any host > 85% GPU util for 10m -> HOLD and scale pool or reduce batch size
- Model routing mismatches: if fallback hit-rate > 5% -> investigate KV cache miss pattern

Telemetry hooks to check immediately after each step
- Dashboard: Release > Canary > Latency p50/p95/p99 (Console route: /console/release/canary-latency)
- Traces: top 10 slow traces in last 15m (Lightstep link in linked_artifacts)
- Logs: grep for OOM/OutOfMemoryError / kernel failures on serving nodes
- Cost: tokens/sec and GPU-hours-per-minute (alert if > budget +25%)

Fast rollback matrix (when to roll back)
- Soft rollback (step back to previous %): non-critical latency spike with no errors
- Hard rollback (remove new model/route): sustained 5xx increase OR complete queueing/backpressure across > 3 hosts
- Emergency kill: repeated crash loops or scheduler evictions in < 10m -> immediate rollback + incident channel runbook

Operator handoff template (for each shift)
- Snapshot time: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC
- Current rollout % and model variant
- Outstanding alerts (names + links)
- Recent mitigations performed and why
- Next scheduled step (time + actor)
- Hot contacts (Discord/Slack handles + phone)

Smoke tests (run after each step)
- /v1/health -> 200, dependencies OK
- 1-sample generation (50 tokens) from canary model -> sanity token count + expected shape
- End-to-end logged request -> confirm prefix KV cache hit improves latency by > 15% for repeat requests
- Embedding job quick check (batch size 128) -> confirm throughput within expected envelope
- Auth & quota check for a known heavy customer -> ensure no sudden throttling

Comms templates (short)
- Slack standup post (use templates in #release-ops):
  "Release lead: {{name}}; Canary -> {{percent}} at {{time}} UTC; Watching p95/5xx. Next step: {{next}} in {{window}}. Dials: batch-size={{n}}; pool={{pool-id}}. Pager if > 5xx spike."
- Customer-facing incident note (first 30m):
  "We are investigating elevated latency for some API requests following a partial rollout. Our engineers are monitoring and will update in 30 minutes. Reference: REL-2389."

Post-release (0–72h) checklist
- [ ] Sweep for regressions with curated evals (prompt/response diffs). Link to evaluation harness in linked_artifacts
- [ ] Confirm canary telemetry remains within SLA windows for 72h
- [ ] Run cost delta report: tokens, GPU hours, infra spend (tagged to this release id)
- [ ] Draft concise release notes and share with product + CS for approval
- [ ] Rotate temporary feature flags and expire any rollout toggles after 7 days

Draft release notes (brief — adapt for product page)
Title: "June 2026: Model routing improvements and canary rollout to reduce tail latency"
Highlights:
- Rolled forward model-routing policy that improves tail latency for repeated context workloads.
- Canary release validated at incremental steps (0.5% -> 100%) with targeted observability.
- No customer-facing errors observed; small latency uplift on one legacy shard rolled back to previous variant.
Known issues:
- Edge case with long-sequence batch shaping caused p99 spikes for a specific job type (tracked REL-2389).
- We reverted one shard temporarily; full fix in progress (PR link GH:repo/inference-server#482).

Notes-to-self / loose questions to follow up:
- Revisit the default canary windows — are we being too aggressive for heavy token workloads?
- Add a lightweight synthetic that simulates prefix-KV warmup patterns for canary traffic.
- Do we want an explicit token-burn throttle during canary for bursty customers?

Quick links and shortcuts (operators)
- Slack: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/release-ops
- PagerDuty schedule: release-oncall
- Canary dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/releases/canary-overview
- GH PR: https://github.com/repo/inference-server/pull/482
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/REL-2389

Field notes (from last rehearsal)
- Observed warmup delta for KV cache ~70s before steady-state latency benefit appears; consider longer observation windows on first two steps.
- When rolling traffic in region eu-west-1 we saw higher token burn due to customer mix — added region-specific throttle.
- Small mislabeling in feature flag caused 10m delay; add feature-flag validation preflight checklist item.

End.
_notes: compact operator-facing doc. intentionally informal; intended to be used on-shift and iterated frequently.
